A library adds **keywords**. A **variable file** adds **variables**. It is a
Python module imported with the `Variables` setting: every module-level name
becomes a Robot Framework variable.

Why not just a `*** Variables ***` section? Because a variable file holds real
Python — lists, dictionaries, values computed at import time — and one file can
be shared across many suites. It is the natural home for configuration: base
URLs, lookup tables, per-environment settings.

## Task 1 — Write a variable file

**Goal:** create `variables/shop_config.py` with three module-level variables — a
scalar `BASE_URL`, a list, and a dictionary `STATUSES`.

Here is the same shape over different data — a warehouse config. Adapt it to the
shop.

<!-- example -->
```python
WAREHOUSE = "eu-west"
ZONES = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
DOCKS = {"inbound": 3, "outbound": 2}
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `variables/shop_config.py` defines `BASE_URL` (and the list and dict).

<!-- hint -->
A variable file is just module-level assignments — no function, no class:
`BASE_URL = "http://localhost:7272"`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Add a list and a dict too — these become `@{...}` and `&{...}` variables:
`CATEGORIES = ["bags", "mugs", "lamps"]` and
`STATUSES = {"complete": "Delivered", "pending": "In transit"}`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```python
BASE_URL = "http://localhost:7272"
CATEGORIES = ["bags", "mugs", "lamps"]
STATUSES = {"complete": "Delivered", "pending": "In transit"}
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Import it and run it green

Create `checks/shop_config.robot`. Import the variable file with `Variables`
(note: not `Library`), then use the variables — including dictionary item access:

```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Variables    ../variables/shop_config.py

*** Test Cases ***
Config Values Resolve
    Should Be Equal    ${BASE_URL}    http://localhost:7272
    Length Should Be    ${CATEGORIES}    3
    Should Be Equal    ${STATUSES}[complete]    Delivered
```

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks/shop_config.robot
```

**Check:** the test `Config Values Resolve` passes.
